items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: But anyway, we went to Madison and we played with Don at a place out there in Madison called the Broadway Gardens.

ctx.x: They played in Kelly's Stables and also the Famous Door, too. But that was when Hawk had a rhythm section and himself and they just added Don. Because Don was such a great player, you know, he really loved Don. But this was before that. I went in Kelly's Stables with Hawk before I went into the radio station.

And the funny thing about it, Hawkins never liked to look back at things, you know. So we used to do an arrangement on -- I was only playing clarinet then, by the way, because we had Hawk and myself and I forget who was playing trumpet at that time. So we were doing -- did the St. Louis Blues. And in rehearsal Hawk said, well, we'll play it with an old ragtime feeling, a corney feeling, and everybody take a ragtime solo, you know. And when they got to his solo he just went on and played, you know. So I said,…
